newsitem.title: USA: Ethics panel votes to release Gingrich report.
newsitem.headline: Ethics panel votes to release Gingrich report.

text.p: The House of Representatives ethics committee voted on Friday to release a long-awaited report on Speaker Newt Gingrich's admitted ethics violations and hold a single hearing on the case later in the day.

The committee's action was announced by Chairwoman Nancy Johnson, a Connecticut Republican, after a closed-door meeting of the committee. The report contains a recommendation for punishment of the speaker.

The report by an investigating subcommittee was drafted by special counsel James Cole who was to have an hour at the open hearing to describe it. A lawyer for Gingrich will make the rebuttal. The meeting was scheduled to begin at 3 p.m. EST (2000 GMT).
Both Johnson and the committee's senior Democrat, Rep. Ben Cardin of Maryland, emphasized that the committee was working cooperatively despite a series of earlier political disputes.

The report is said to recommend a reprimand for the speaker, a stiff fine -- over $100,000 according to some news reports -- and a call for a full federal investigation on the apparent use of charitable contributions for partisan political purposes.

The ethics committee, which is divided equally between Republicans and Democrats, is to give the full House its recommendation on what punishments to levy against Gingrich, a Republican. The House is scheduled to vote on that issue next Tuesday.
